questions.stem: What is the most reliable indicator of a client's pain?

options.text: The nurse's estimate based on the procedure

rationale.correct: Self-report is the gold standard; use behavioral scales when the client can't report.

perOption.a: Pain is whatever the client says it is.
perOption.b: Expressions vary and can be misleading.
perOption.c: Vital signs may not change with chronic pain.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Identify the most reliable pain indicator.

questions.stem: How should the nurse assess pain in a client with advanced dementia who can't give a self-report?

options.text: Use a behavioral pain scale such as PAINAD
Assume the client has no pain
Ask the client to rate pain from 0 to 10

rationale.correct: Use validated behavioral scales for nonverbal clients.

perOption.a: Behavioral scales assess breathing, vocalization, facial expression, body language and consolability.
perOption.b: Pain is often undertreated in dementia.
perOption.c: The client can't use a numeric scale.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Assess pain in a client with dementia.

questions.stem: A client sprained an ankle 2 hours ago. Which comfort measure is best?

options.text: A cold pack for 15 to 20 minutes at a time

rationale.correct: Use cold for acute injuries in the first 24 to 48 hours, heat later; limit applications to 15 to 20 minutes.

perOption.a: Cold reduces swelling and pain in the first 24 to 48 hours.
perOption.b: Heat increases swelling in an acute injury.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Choose heat or cold therapy appropriately.

questions.stem: A client taking sertraline says they've started St. John's wort. Why is the nurse concerned?

options.text: The combination can cause serotonin syndrome
St. John's wort lowers blood glucose

rationale.correct: St. John's wort interacts with SSRIs (serotonin syndrome) and reduces the effect of many drugs, such as oral contraceptives and warfarin.

perOption.a: Both increase serotonin.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client says, "I'd like to use acupuncture along with my medicine for back pain." What is the nurse's best response?

options.text: "Let's tell your provider so your care can be coordinated."
"Do whatever you like without telling anyone."

rationale.correct: Support complementary therapies while making sure the provider knows and screening for interactions.

perOption.a: This respects the client's choice and supports safe, coordinated care.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Respond to interest in complementary therapy.

questions.stem: The nurse is teaching sleep hygiene. Which statement shows a need for more teaching?

options.text: "I'll go to bed at the same time each night."
"I'll watch TV in bed until I fall asleep."
"I'll keep my bedroom cool and dark."

rationale.correct: Sleep hygiene: consistent schedule, bed for sleep only, limit caffeine, alcohol and screens.

perOption.a: A consistent schedule supports sleep.
perOption.c: Screens and non-sleep activities in bed disrupt sleep.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: An 82-year-old client asks for a sleeping pill. What is the nurse's main concern about sedative-hypnotics in older adults?

options.text: Increased risk of falls and confusion

rationale.correct: Avoid sedative-hypnotics in older adults when possible; try non-drug measures first.

perOption.a: Sedatives impair balance and cognition in older adults (Beers criteria).

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize the risks of sedatives in older adults.

questions.stem: A client is on a clear liquid diet. Which item can the nurse offer?

rationale.correct: Clear liquids: water, broth, clear juice, gelatin, popsicles. Full liquids add milk, pudding and ice cream.

perOption.a: Clear liquids are transparent at room temperature.
perOption.d: Ice cream is a full liquid.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Choose foods for a clear liquid diet.

questions.stem: Which lunch choice is best for a client on a low-sodium diet?

options.text: Grilled fresh chicken with steamed vegetables

rationale.correct: Low sodium: choose fresh foods; limit canned, cured, processed and fast foods.

perOption.a: Fresh, unprocessed foods are low in sodium.
perOption.c: Cured meats and pickles are high in sodium.
perOption.d: Processed foods are high in sodium.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client with celiac disease is choosing foods. Which choice is safe?

rationale.correct: Celiac disease: avoid wheat, barley and rye; rice, corn and certified gluten-free oats are safe.

perOption.a: Rice is naturally gluten-free.

references: Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which food is highest in fiber?

rationale.correct: High-fiber foods: legumes, whole grains, fruits, vegetables, bran.

perOption.a: Legumes are high in fiber.
perOption.b: Refined grains are low in fiber.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client weighs 90 kg and is 1.75 m tall. What is the client's body mass index (BMI)? Round to the nearest tenth.

rationale.correct: BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)² = 90 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 90 ÷ 3.0625 = 29.4 (overweight range: 25 to 29.9).
references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: How should the nurse provide oral care to an unconscious client?

options.text: Turn the client to the side, have suction ready and use a soft toothette
Keep the client flat and pour water into the mouth to rinse
Skip oral care because the client isn't eating
Use a hard toothbrush and lots of toothpaste

rationale.correct: Oral care for unconscious clients: side-lying, minimal fluid, suction available.

perOption.a: Side-lying and suction prevent aspiration.
perOption.c: Oral care prevents infection and pneumonia.
perOption.d: This can injure tissue and cause aspiration.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Provide safe oral care to an unconscious client.

questions.stem: A client with dementia becomes agitated during the morning shower. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Be flexible: try a towel bath or a different time of day
Insist on completing the shower right away

rationale.correct: Person-centered care in dementia: flexibility, simple steps, calm approach.

perOption.a: Adjusting the approach reduces distress while meeting hygiene needs.
perOption.d: Hygiene needs must still be met.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Adapt hygiene care for a client with dementia.

questions.stem: How should the nurse store a client's dentures overnight?

options.text: In a labeled denture cup with water or cleaning solution
Wrapped in a paper towel on the meal tray

rationale.correct: Denture care: clean over a padded sink and store in a labeled cup with liquid.

perOption.a: This prevents warping and loss.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which complications can result from prolonged immobility? Select all that apply.

rationale.correct: Immobility affects every system: skin, circulation, lungs, bowels, muscles and bones.

perOption.a: Constant pressure reduces blood flow to the skin.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: When performing passive range-of-motion exercises, what should the nurse do?

options.text: Support the joint above and below and stop at the point of resistance or pain
Move each joint past the point of pain

rationale.correct: Passive ROM: slow, supported and within comfort.

perOption.a: This prevents injury.
perOption.d: All joints need ROM unless contraindicated.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which intervention helps prevent foot drop in a client on prolonged bed rest?

options.text: High-top sneakers or a foot board to keep the feet at 90 degrees
Tucking the sheets tightly over the toes

rationale.correct: Prevent foot drop with neutral ankle positioning and ROM.

perOption.a: This keeps the ankles in a neutral position.
perOption.c: This pushes the feet into plantar flexion.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is helping a client with right-sided weakness move from the bed to a wheelchair. Place the steps in order.

items.text: Place the wheelchair on the client's left (strong) side at a slight angle and lock the brakes
Apply a gait belt around the client's waist
Help the client sit on the edge of the bed with feet flat on the floor
Help the client stand and pivot on the strong leg
Lower the client into the wheelchair

rationale.correct: Transfer toward the strong side with locked brakes and a gait belt.

perOption.a: The client moves toward the strong side, with the chair secured.
perOption.b: Sitting first lets the blood pressure adjust.
perOption.c: The belt gives the nurse a secure hold.
perOption.d: Pivoting on the strong leg is safest.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Transfer a client from bed to wheelchair safely.

questions.stem: When is the best time for a client in a bowel training program to try to have a bowel movement?

options.text: Only when the client feels the urge
On an empty stomach before breakfast

rationale.correct: Bowel training: same time daily, after a meal, with fiber and fluids.

perOption.a: The gastrocolic reflex after meals stimulates peristalsis.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which intervention is most appropriate for an older adult with functional urinary incontinence?

rationale.correct: Incontinence care: scheduled toileting, easy access to the toilet and skin protection.

perOption.a: Regular toileting reduces accidents.
perOption.b: This increases infection risk and isn't first-line.
perOption.c: This causes dehydration and concentrated urine.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.stem: While removing a fecal impaction digitally, the nurse notes the client's heart rate drops from 78 to 48/min. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Stop the procedure and assess the client
Lower the head of the bed and keep going

rationale.correct: Digital removal can stimulate the vagus nerve; stop if bradycardia occurs.

perOption.a: Rectal stimulation can trigger a vagal response with bradycardia.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize a vagal response during digital disimpaction.

questions.stem: A client's feeding tube is clogged. What should the nurse try first?

options.text: Flush gently with warm water using a 30 to 60 mL syringe
Insert a stylet to push through the clog
Use a small syringe with high pressure

rationale.correct: Prevent clogs with regular water flushes; clear them gently with warm water.

perOption.a: Warm water is the first-line way to clear a clog.
perOption.b: Acidic drinks can make clogs worse.
perOption.c: This can perforate the tube or GI tract.
perOption.d: Small syringes create high pressure that can rupture the tube.

references: Fundamentals of nursing texts (e.g. Potter & Perry)
Reviewed by the content team on 17 November 2026.
